findings.rationale: A request command excludes only Pending and Succeeded, so the same correlation can re-enter from Failed or TimedOut and reset its attempt count to 1. Reinvoking the original command therefore bypasses the retry action's max-attempts guard indefinitely.

Completion is authorized solely by correlation status being Pending; the current attempt number is neither accepted nor checked. After a retry, a delayed response from an earlier attempt can therefore complete the newer attempt.

Awaits are omitted whenever a step emits, and generated step and timeout actions record no started/completed phase. Such actions can execute before the awaited outcome and can be invoked repeatedly whenever their remaining static guards hold; normal and timeout transitions may also be enabled together.

Every event is represented by one global Boolean and saga actions have no instance or correlation key. Concurrent saga instances can consume each other's events, and an all-await over events arriving in separate transitions cannot accumulate because every action clears prior flags.

The compensation's after_event is used only in the generated action name and observer collection; its sole guard checks trigger_event. Compensation can consequently run even when the forward event it is declared to follow never occurred.

Saga steps and compensations only set event flags. Unlike command emission, they neither apply the emitted event's aggregate evolution nor initialize matching effect status and attempts. A saga-emitted effect request can remain NotStarted, making every completion action's Pending guard unreachable.

Enum comparisons are rewritten with unrestricted string replacement. If one member is a prefix of another, such as A before AB, normalizing `x == AB` can first replace `x == A` and produce a malformed or incorrect token sequence.

Default generation handles only Bool, Int, and named enum/range/external/value-object types; every other type falls back to `0`. A Map, Set, Seq, Option, or other supported composite state field without an explicit default is therefore initialized with an incompatible integer literal.
